headline: A thousand buttons cycling twelve class strings put nine lanes within 16% of each other, because almost every lookup is a cache hit; the split is between lanes that cache and lanes that recompute regardless.

top3.label: StyleX without CSS layers (:not() specificity hack)

microbench.why: Roughly twelve distinct class strings serve 1,000 buttons, so most calls hit a cache and the case prices lookup rather than style computation. Nine lanes finish between 1.24M and 1.76M renders/s, led by `next-yak-css` at 1.76M with each variant condition compiled into a ternary over literal class names. `stylex` at 1.73M and `cnfast` at 1.72M sit in the same band because their merge is a map lookup on repeated keys. The lanes that fall away are the ones that recompute whatever the repetition: `next-yak-nofold` at 782,000 builds a wrapper per instance, `panda` at 795,000 re-resolves its style object, and `emotion` at 353,000 re-serializes from scratch.

autocannon.why: `next-yak` leads at 1,595 req/s with `vanilla` at 1,431. The instructive pair is inside Panda: `panda-recipe` at 928 req/s does 1.6× the work of `panda` at 590 on the same variants, because a recipe resolves its variant table during the build rather than on every call.

attribution.why: Six lanes total between 0.653 ms and 0.731 ms, which is the floor for 1,000 single-element buttons. `next-yak-css` books 0.000 ms of lib self-time, `next-yak` books 0.286 ms and still totals 0.664 ms, and `next-yak-nofold` doubles the total to 1.32 ms on identical source with folding off. `emotion` at 3.02 ms and `goober` at 2.09 ms carry their serializers into every instance.

hydrate.why: `next-yak` hydrates fastest at 42.2 ms, with six lanes under 47 ms. `next-yak-css-nofold` at 91.8 ms is the outlier inside its own family, twice its folded sibling's 45.0 ms, because every variant condition turns back into a runtime merge while the client walks the tree. `emotion` at 114 ms and `styled-components` at 92.0 ms rebuild sheets first.

inp.why: Fifteen lanes answer one click between 7.2 ms and 7.8 ms, indistinguishable at this spread. `emotion` at 10.9 ms is the only lane that separates.

top3.label: StyleX without CSS layers (:not() specificity hack)

mount.why: Twelve lanes mount between 68.5 ms and 89.0 ms. The 29.1 ms recorded for `stylex-layers` is a sampling artifact rather than a result: that cell is bimodal, its samples run from 27 ms to 86 ms, and the second run puts its median at 70.3 ms in line with everyone else.

renderTiming.why: One style recalculation per lane, 0.127 ms to 0.218 ms. Twelve distinct class strings over one element per instance give the engine the same matching work everywhere.

payload.why: `next-yak-css` ships 3,737 gz B against 4,540 B for `next-yak`, the difference being the wrapper runtime. `panda-recipe` at 6,477 B carries 1,442 B of JS, under a third of `panda`'s 4,903 B, because the recipe's variant table is resolved during the build instead of shipped as a resolver. The utility and runtime lanes run from 15.1 kB to 17.0 kB.

top3.label: StyleX without CSS layers (:not() specificity hack)

nsweep.why: `next-yak` holds 1.91 ms at the largest size while `next-yak-nofold` needs 5.06 ms, a 2.65× gap that widens with the count because the wrapper runs per instance however repetitive the variants are. `emotion` at 11.2 ms sets the far end.
